A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SmartBench. Their main texts, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched, including relocated and renumbered examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, quantized smartphone inference experiments, and human-ranking validation in Section 4 and Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds GPT-4o scores, smartphone speed and power measurements, expanded human validation, and supplementary comparisons.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction workflow and task-specific LLM-as-a-Judge procedure remain unchanged. The added screening thresholds and generation prompt document the existing process without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds an MMLU objective-knowledge comparison for Qwen2.5-3B and InternVL2.5-4B. SmartBench itself retains the same 2,973 QA pairs, five categories, and 20 Chinese smartphone tasks.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds GPT-4o as a cloud reference alongside the five existing on-device models. The human-validation comparison and Qwen-Max-judged tables retain their original comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 expands the reported human-validation sample from 20 to 50 questions per task, increasing evaluated model responses from 2,000 to 5,000. v2 also adds a separate evaluation of prefilling speed, output speed, and power at context length 2,048 (Table 5). Existing BF16 and W4A16 benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.4 contrasts objective-knowledge and subjective-alignment rankings for two models. Appendix A.5 adds two before/after quantization cases illustrating degraded fluency and contextual understanding. Existing judge comparisons, quantization results, and other qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use Pearson correlation for human-ranking agreement without reported confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run uncertainty estimates. Increasing the number of sampled questions changes evaluation size, not the statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds GPT-4o results averaging 7.37, MMLU scores of 66.31 for Qwen2.5-3B and 68.35 for InternVL2.5-4B, and smartphone speed/power results. Under the enlarged human-validation sample, average correlations change from 0.8260 to 0.8280 for SmartBench and 0.7970 to 0.7959 for MT-Bench; these are replaced results under different sample sizes. All original on-device scores in the main and appendix benchmark tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. The added screening thresholds are procedural details, and the new benchmark discussion is empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a Chinese smartphone benchmark with 20 tasks and 2,973 QA pairs, tailored automated evaluation, and on-device model assessment. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 discusses the cloud-model gap, qualifies approximately 90% quantization retention with concrete failures, and expands the interpretation of objective knowledge versus subjective alignment. It also explicitly identifies text-only coverage as a limitation. These additions refine the retained conclusions and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly specifies five-point screening scales, a 3.5 retention threshold, manual relabeling between 3.5 and 4, and reduction from roughly 30,000 candidates to 3,000 entries. Appendix A.6 supplies a detailed notification-generation prompt. These substantially expand construction documentation. v2 also reports efficiency settings and changes the advertised repository from Lucky-Lance/SmartBench to vivo-ai-lab/SmartBench.

R1.justification: Section 2.4 adds Rawles et al.'s AndroidWorld citation. Appendix A.4 further illustrates the existing distinction from objective-knowledge benchmarks, while the claimed Chinese smartphone-assistance niche remains unchanged. Most other reference edits are bibliographic formatting.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. v2 expands screening explanations and experimental discussion, adds three appendix subsections, and makes limited wording and author-contact edits; it does not substantially rewrite the narrative.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains a GPT-4o column. v2 adds the efficiency table, an unnumbered MMLU comparison table, and Figures 5–7 for failure cases and a generation prompt. Existing figures retain their content with renumbering and limited layout changes, including single-column formatting for some appendix prose.

improvement.justification: Explicit screening rules and a generation prompt improve transparency, while larger human validation, a cloud reference, and quantization failure cases strengthen the evaluation context. These are useful incremental gains over v1's retained benchmark evidence. The new MMLU comparison lacks protocol detail and controlled support for its causal interpretation, limiting the strength of that addition.
